metas.name: Akureyri - City
metas.note: Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a North-South oriented valley, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the east and west, making it recognisable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Dark Gravel - Landscape
metas.note: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Flat - Landscape
metas.note: The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Flat Mountains - Mountains
metas.note: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Fog - Spotlight
metas.note: Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Forest - Landscape
metas.note: The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Glacier - Spotlight
metas.note: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Heimaey - Spotlight
metas.note: The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Highway - Spotlight
metas.note:
There are only a handful of highways in Iceland which are either divided or have more than two lanes. The divided highways are shown in dark red, while the highways with three or more lanes are shown in bright red.

NOTE: There are two exceptions to this:

Divided roads can be found inside cities other than Reykjavík.

Roads may temporarily be divided close to intersections.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Jagged Mountains - Mountains
metas.note: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Lake - Landscape
metas.note: There a few locations, with a huge lake. They look like a Fjord, but if you zoom to the other side, you will see more mountains.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Ocean Site - Ocean Site
metas.note: Many places in Iceland look the same, but in some places you can clearly see the ocean. If you align your compass with it, you can determine the approximate side of Iceland you are on. But be careful, don't be confused by fjords.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Reykjavik - City
metas.note:
Reykjavík is the capital and by far the largest city in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and “bigger city” feel.

NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Roadnumber - Roadnumbers
metas.note:
Iceland has a very sensible road numbering system that allows for quick 5k’s, provided you find the yellow direction signs that list the road numbers of the intersection you are on.

The main ring road, which circles the entire island, simply has the number 1. There are no other roads that start with 1.

The first digit of the other road numbers is region-specific. These regions have a sequential distribution around the island, starting from 2 in the south and increasing up until 9 in a clockwise direction (see map for approximate distribution).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Valley - Landscape
metas.note: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Wide Valley - Landscape
metas.note: The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
